newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea prices stabilise on Russian buying.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea prices stabilise on Russian buying.

text.p: Tea prices stabilised at the Colombo tea auction on Wednesday on a recovery by better quality high and medium growns, brokers said.
"Medium and high grown liquoring teas, which have fallen for the last two weeks, stabilised due to Russian buying," said Lalith Ramanayake, managing director of produce brokers John Keells Ltd.
The price per kg rose to between 94 and 95 rupees from around 92 to 93 rupees last week, he said.
"Better quality high grown teas also rose sharply by an average of five to 10 rupees a kg," he added.
Low grown teas remained soft as a market correction, which began after prices hit a high of 193.04 rupees a kg in June, continued, brokers said.
"But the interesting thing here was that the price of good low growns were buoyant while the bad ones fell," said Ramanayake.
The anticipated average auction price for the 5.9 million kg on offer was 114.25 rupees ($1.95) per kg, as gainst 114.71 last week, said produce brokers Forbes & Walker.
The next auction is on July 22-23 when 6.3 million kg will be on offer. ($=58.50).
